prompt:
Show an actual editable timeline as the dominant form, with one mountain shot and two product shots, short caption track blocks, a voiceover waveform and a single rendered export frame. Avoid form-like cards and dummy text. Keep inputs and an approved export visible as physical film/paper illustrations, not realistic scenery. Only the exact approved labels in the supplied list may be printed, and no code or source quotes. Approval is a human workflow step. No people, body parts or product logos.
Create one beautiful professional technical-book editorial illustration with white paper, 1200 by 630 landscape. Art-direct as a professional film-editing desk sheet viewed directly from overhead. One generated mountain shot joins an existing timeline, with visible edits in the clip sequence, caption, voiceover and audio tracks. The join between the editable project and export is a clear visual cut. Present approval as an editorial review practice rather than a built-in product lock. No logos, generic UI cards, invented small lettering or unlisted controls. Use Orthographic overhead and Graphite and vermilion. Depict only the source facts: A Video Studio clip reaches the main track in the online editor. Editors can combine own clips, voiceover and captions with a generated shot. A project keeps editorial changes available before export. Preserve very large print labels with a 72 px inset; source detail on every meaningful surface. Required visible text exactly once each: Generated shot | Video track | Voiceover | Captions | Editable project | Review edits | Export | Editor review step. Draw only the named connections at object ports, separate caveat, no caption strip, no badge wall, no other text or frame. Geometry below is for art direction and must never appear printed.
